title: Zupka · dark-only workspace
question: Choose the direction for the owner’s content workspace. These are visual studies with illustrative entries, not live CMS data.

options.label: Field Atlas
options.thesis: A forest-dark workspace where draft and public versions are easy to distinguish.
options.viewport: Content-type sidebar, Posts heading and search above a generous entry table; version markers explain each publication state.
options.risk: The version markers must reinforce plain-language states, never become a code to learn.

raised.raise: Preserve strict title/state/date alignment even with long titles.
Make selection unmistakable without relying on hover.
Separate primary titles from supporting slugs through a disciplined type hierarchy.
Give navigation a committed field of colour, not scattered accents.
Make version markers secondary to the entry title, with a consistent visual vocabulary.

options.label: Gallery Index
options.thesis: A plum-dark, title-led workspace that gives writing room to breathe.
options.viewport: A restrained sidebar and title-first list; search and status filters stay close to the entries, with textual states beside each title.
options.risk: Familiar and effective; less distinctive than the atlas, and fewer entries fit on screen.

options.label: Publication Board
options.lineage: Gate-board information hierarchy, without airport decoration
options.thesis: A dense, blue-black entry table with persistent amber emphasis for unpublished changes.
options.viewport: Top content-type navigation, compact search and filters, then an aligned title/state/updated table; draft changes remain visibly marked.
options.case: Competitive on product clarity: exceptionally scannable states; weaker audience identification because a writing space can feel operational.
options.risk: Could feel like monitoring software rather than a place for authored content.

options.label: Concourse Board
options.thesis: A compact table borrowing disciplined columns, not letter-flip theatre.
options.case: Less suited to authored work and less explicit about draft/public versions than Field Atlas.
options.risk: Rigid density can crowd long titles.
options.viewport: Content-type navigation and a filtered entry list, without literal source-world controls.

options.label: Character Catalogue
options.thesis: A dark roster with strongly selected entry cells.
options.case: Portrait-led identification fits neither arbitrary custom content types nor text-only entries; clarity and audience fit both fall below Field Atlas.
options.risk: Entry portraits would imply imagery that may not exist.
options.viewport: Content-type navigation and a filtered entry list, without literal source-world controls.

options.label: Reference Edition
options.thesis: A dark reading-first list with fine typographic hierarchy.
options.case: Its reading apparatus is less natural for entry management and makes publication states harder to scan than Field Atlas.
options.risk: Book-like density and small apparatus can weaken accessibility.
options.viewport: Content-type navigation and a filtered entry list, without literal source-world controls.

options.label: Garden Guide
options.thesis: A dark colour-zoned workspace using standard list controls.
options.case: Large colour areas identify places better than authored entries; both audience fit and state clarity are weaker than Field Atlas.
options.risk: Colourful zones can distract from entry titles.
options.kept: Colour commitment across the navigation region.
options.viewport: Content-type navigation and a filtered entry list, without literal source-world controls.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: A navy list with ranked markers and subtle version rings.
options.case: Spatial magnitude has no truthful entry equivalent; a standard list with secondary markers is clearer and closer to the owner's work.
options.risk: Decorative plotting would suggest a nonexistent relationship between entries.
options.viewport: Content-type navigation and a filtered entry list, without literal source-world controls.

canonCard.label: Familiar dark admin
canonCard.thesis: The category standard: neutral charcoal, a compact sidebar, conventional table and blue selection.
canonCard.viewport: Content-type sidebar, search and status filters, title/state/date table, pagination.
canonCard.risk: Deliberately familiar rather than recognisably Zupka.
